title: Docs Site: SDK release windows, canaries, and hotfix playbook
author: Lena Zhou
content:
Overview

This page defines the operational pattern the Docs Site and SDK teams use for planned SDK releases, weekly docs site change windows, canary promotion, and expedited hotfixes. The goal is to minimize user-facing regressions, speed up critical fixes, and keep rollout telemetry auditable. This playbook is intended for library authors, Docs Site maintainers, DevX oncall, and Release Engineers.

When to follow this playbook

- Regular SDK releases (minor/patch) that change public APIs or default runtime behavior.
- Docs Site content or snippet changes that must be synchronized with an SDK release.
- Hotfixes that restore regressions in production (build failures, telemetry regressions, wrong default params).
- Emergency rollbacks when a release causes production errors exceeding alert thresholds.

Release cadence and windows

- Regular release window: Tuesdays 10:00–12:00 PT. Use this window for scheduled minor and patch SDK releases and docs content pushes.
- Docs-only window: Wednesdays 14:00–15:00 PT for non-SDK content updates that still require minimal review.
- Hotfix window: 24/7 — hotfixes may be requested outside scheduled windows but must follow the expedited verification checklist below.

Roles and responsibilities

- Release owner (library author): creates the release PR, runs preflight checks, and opens the rollout ticket.
- Docs Site owner (docs-maintainer): coordinates snippet updates, staging verification, and monitors site health dashboards.
- DevX oncall: monitors canary telemetry and approves promotion; executes rollback when thresholds are met.
- Release engineer: validates CI gates and can trigger the automated promotion pipeline.

Pre-release checklist (required before merging a release PR)

1) Update changelog and API compatibility note. Include the minimal reproduction for behavior changes.
2) Run the local integration matrix: node, python, and go SDK quickstart smoke tests (see sample commands below).
3) Run docs build: ensure snippet extraction and the docs site staging build succeed (docs build exit code == 0).
4) Verify telemetry: run unit and integration tests that exercised telemetry counters and ensure no new missing telemetry keys.
5) Attach a release ticket with: expected impact, canary group definition, and rollback plan.

Canary promotion flow (recommended for all production-impacting changes)

1) Create a canary release artifact tagged with the date and canary identifier (e.g., sdk-js@2.5.1-canary-20250212-rc1).
2) Stage docs site with canary artifact references in a per-canary branch of the staging site.
3) Run the canary smoke suite (minimum: 50 requests across the common endpoints, latency and correctness checks).
4) Monitor the following metrics for 30 minutes:
   - error_rate (requests with 5xx or SDK-level errors) < 0.5%
   - median_latency (p50) change <= +15% relative to baseline
   - token_cost_per_request change <= +30% relative to baseline (for generation endpoints)
   - golden_prompt_accuracy: local eval against 100 golden prompts must not regress >1% absolute
5) If all checks pass, request approval from DevX oncall and merge to main release track. Record approval in the release ticket.

Hotfix (expedited) flow

1) Triage: engineer files an incident ticket and labels it hotfix. Capture: failing endpoint, example request, last-good-artifact, and impact estimate (users/minute affected).
2) Create a hotfix branch off the last-good-artifact and implement the minimal change.
3) Run focused tests: the hotfix test suite must include the failure repro and must pass locally and in CI smoke.
4) Deploy to a canary cohort of 1% traffic for 10 minutes. If no new errors and all validation checks pass, incrementally increase to 10% for 20 minutes.
5) If at any point error_rate > 1% or latency p50 increases > 30% vs baseline, immediately rollback to last-good-artifact and escalate to Incident Commander.

Rollback procedure (when rolling back a failed release)

1) Post the rollback plan in the release ticket and on the incident channel.
2) Run the automated rollback pipeline to restore last-good-artifact.
3) Clear caches (docs snippet cache, CDN edge purge) where applicable.
4) Run post-rollback smoke checks and monitor metrics for 60 minutes.
5) Create a postmortem entry if rollback was performed (link the incident ticket).

Monitoring and SLOs for SDK and Docs changes

- Canary pass rate: target 99% pass for smoke checks prior to promotion.
- Production error rate SLO (post-release 6h window): increase in error_rate must be <= 0.25% absolute from baseline; otherwise trigger rollback.
- Docs build success: 100% during release window. Any docs build failures must block promotion.

Observability and dashboards to watch

- docs-site/staging-builds: build status, snippet-extraction errors, last successful build time.
- sdk/canary-health: error_rate, p50/p95 latencies, token_cost_per_request, golden_eval_regressions.
- synthetic/quickstarts: scheduled runs of the standard quickstarts (node, python, go) every 30 minutes.

Templates and sample commands

- Local quickstart smoke (Node):
  npm ci && npm run smoke -- --endpoint=https://staging.docs.redwood.ai --api-key=${API_KEY}

- Local quickstart smoke (Python):
  pip install -r requirements.txt && python smoke_quickstart.py --endpoint https://staging.docs.redwood.ai --api_key $API_KEY

- Example CI job snippet (concise):
  - name: SDK smoke tests
    run: |
      make smoke-node && make smoke-py && make docs-build

- Canary tagging convention: sdk-{lang}@{version}-canary-{YYYYMMDD}-{build}

Ownership matrix

- Release owner: SDK library team (primary)
- Docs maintenance: Docs Site engineering (primary), DevX (secondary)
- Oncall verification: DevX oncall (primary)
- Rollback execution: Release engineering (primary)

Post-release responsibilities and runbook triggers

- 0–6 hours after release: active monitoring window. Oncall checks dashboards every 15 minutes.
- If error_rate breach occurs: trigger rollback runbook and create an incident ticket.
- >6 hours and <72 hours: monitoring at 1-hour cadence; file a regression ticket if behavioral regressions are observed.

Common pitfalls and canonical fixes

- Problem: snippets in docs reference unreleased helper APIs.
  Fix: add feature gates to the staging build and keep snippet references behind canary tags until SDK promotion.
- Problem: CI passes locally but fails in docs build due to missing environment variables.
  Fix: use the standardized docs stub env and add a gating CI job that runs the docs build with secrets masked.
- Problem: golden prompt regressions aren’t caught until late.
  Fix: add a lightweight golden set for each SDK and run a differential eval in the canary stage.

Appendix: example changelog template

- Title: sdk-{lang} v{major}.{minor}.{patch} — YYYY-MM-DD
- Summary: One-line summary of impact.
- Notable changes:
  - Breaking changes: list and migration steps
  - Bug fixes: list of tickets and short descriptions
  - Docs changes: list of pages/snippets updated

Troubleshooting checklist (quick)

1) If docs site staging build fails: check snippet-extraction logs, missing env, and plugin versions.
2) If canary shows increased latency: check kernel selection logs, batching metrics, and upstream model variant routing.
3) If golden accuracy regresses: revert the SDK change and re-run local evals; open an evaluation ticket with the Research Applied ML team.

Contact and escalation

- Primary Slack channel: #devx-release-ops
- Oncall rotation: see /confluence/eng-developer-experience/oncall-and-rotations (link)
- Pager: DevX oncall; Release engineering backup: release@redwood.ai
